indicator_definition: This indicator measures the share of 15-year-old students who fail to reach level 2 (minimum level of proficiency) in reading, mathematics and science, based on the OECD Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). It is expressed as a percentage of all students assessed.
rationale: Ensuring that all young people acquire minimum literacy and numeracy skills is fundamental to quality education. High rates of underachievement limit future employment and economic participation. Progress means reducing the share of low-achieving students in all three domains.
methodology_characteristics: Data come from the OECD PISA survey, conducted every three years among students aged 15. Level 2 proficiency is the baseline level at which students begin to demonstrate competencies that enable them to participate actively in modern society. The survey covers reading, mathematics and science.
indicator_name: Low achieving students in reading, mathematics and science
graph_title: Low achieving students in reading, mathematics and science
